title: Spot the Flaw: Governance & Contracts Edition
brief: This customer-360 model is heading to production behind a data contract. It is structurally sound and correctly named, but a governance review flagged three gaps that would ship a weak contract: a Tier-1 critical asset with no freshness SLA, an unclassified PII column, and an undocumented dimension. Fix all three in-app, then re-validate to see the contract go clean.

expected_flaws.hint: A Tier-1 critical asset with no freshness guarantee makes a hollow contract. Which asset promises freshness but declares none?
expected_flaws.fix: Open fact_orders' entity settings and declare a freshness SLA, e.g. '< 1h'.

expected_flaws.hint: The contract must declare which columns carry personal data. One column looks like PII but isn't classified.
expected_flaws.fix: Select dim_customer.email and tick 'Contains PII' (pii_type EMAIL) so the contract governs it.

expected_flaws.hint: A consumer can't sign a contract against an undocumented asset. Which dimension has no description?
expected_flaws.fix: Open dim_marketing's entity settings and write a description.

solution_notes: The contract-ready model declares a freshness SLA on the Tier-1 fact_orders asset, classifies dim_customer.email as PII (EMAIL), and documents dim_marketing. All three fixes are made with the in-app editors — Entity Settings for the SLA and description, the column editor's 'Contains PII' toggle for the classification. After the fixes, re-validation shows no MISSING_SLA, PII_EXPOSURE, or MISSING_DESCRIPTION issues, and the exported OpenDataContract/dbt artifacts carry the tier, slaProperties, and PII metadata.
